title: P43: depth-scaled initialization of residual output projections
description: P43: divide the initial attention-output and MLP-output weight matrices in each of the four blocks by sqrt(8), leaving every other parameter and the RNG stream unchanged. Smaller initial residual updates may establish proof features that the fixed downstream expert-iteration procedure can extend more effectively.
hypothesis: The incumbent initializes all linear weights with standard deviation 0.02 regardless of residual depth. Reducing only the eight residual-output matrices to standard deviation about 0.007071 may improve early signal propagation and the learned starting policy for RL without reducing unique capacity. Prior runs with reduced-capacity sharing (014), altered second moments (015), smoothing (017), selective decay (018), and more heads (019) failed to beat the incumbent; none tested initialization. This intervention also reduces initial gradients through the corresponding branches and could slow feature learning. Downstream dev-transfer >=7 performance alone determines keep/discard; lower pretraining loss is only diagnostic.
expected_delta: Central prediction +5 to +15 dev-transfer theorems at true length >=7 versus baseline 012 (exact mean 147.67, stored rounded mean 148), with plausible downside -35. Keep only if the mean on seeds 0,1,2 improves. Eight one-time in-place matrix divisions should have negligible budget cost; parameter count, forward computation and expected pretraining throughput remain approximately unchanged (about 3000 steps in 300 seconds). Learned generation lengths can still change downstream latency under the fixed 1200-second cap.

config.init: Fork default normal std=0.02, then divide each block.proj.weight and block.fc2.weight by sqrt(2*N_LAYER)=sqrt(8); resulting std about 0.007071. All other weights and biases unchanged, no extra RNG draws.

residual_init.handoff: ordinary GPT weights; no runtime residual scaling or RL optimizer changes
